speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since your episode resolved quickly and you are currently at baseline, did you notice any specific triggers, such as rolling over in bed or looking up, that initiated the spinning? Also, do you have any history of neck injuries or recent head trauma?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness.

text: To confirm my suspicion of Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo, I need to observe your eye movements and symptoms during specific head maneuvers. REQUEST TEST: Dix-Hallpike maneuver.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Dix-Hallpike_Manoeuvre: Positive, inducing nystagmus and reproducing patient’s symptoms of vertigo when head is turned to the left and laid back.

speaker: Doctor
text: The positive Dix-Hallpike maneuver confirming your symptoms and nystagmus allows me to finalize the assessment. DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV) of the left posterior semicircular canal.
